# `remote_join`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Join the device to a remote (cloud relay) service using supplied credentials.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe37c0, ParserRemoteJoin @0xd9ed0, RemoteJoin @0x1a2260 (64-bit build); firmware 9.75 (app 3.4.0, 64-bit build) cloud-link resolver report |

Parses the credentials, fetches the access-point SSID (which may refresh access-point caches), fills the native connection info and delegates to the remote-join library call, waiting up to timeout_sec seconds for it to return. On success the original request text is written to the stored remote-join file and a joined-state change is broadcast. The reply is a bare success. The remote protocol, total blocking time and connection preconditions are unresolved. A failed save of the stored file does not change the success reply. Firmware 9.75 (64-bit build, READ), the request handling and error codes are unchanged. The remote-join library call and the P2P status upload are described in spec/auth/cloud-auth/device-cloud-link.md.

Side effects: Writes the remote-join request file, may refresh access-point caches, and broadcasts changed join state; may block for the timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"remote_join"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Remote (cloud relay) join credentials. Object form only: the credential parser reads named members, so no successful positional spelling is established. All five credential members are required strings; any missing or wrong-typed one fails the whole parse with code 259. No non-empty or numeric-range check is made in the immediate parser. Unknown keys are ignored. The companion app sends exactly the five credential members. [READ] |
| `params.host` | string | yes | - | Relay host name. [READ] |
| `params.productKey` | string | yes | - | Relay product key. [READ] |
| `params.deviceName` | string | yes | - | Relay device name. [READ] |
| `params.deviceSecret` | string | yes | - | Relay device secret. Sensitive; not logged here. [READ] |
| `params.port` | string | yes | - | Relay port, sent as a string, not a number. [READ] |
| `params.timeout_sec` | integer | no | 2 | Seconds the handler waits for the join call to return; multiplied by 1000 in a signed int with no clamp (overflow behaviour unresolved). Wrong type fails with 104. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | timeout_sec present but not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 259 | Any credential parse failure (missing or non-string member, or non-object params); the message is misleading | `stack is already running` |
| 207 | The join call returned nonzero | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, join - Placeholder credentials:

```json
{"id":60,"method":"remote_join","params":{"host":"relay.example.invalid","productKey":"EXAMPLEKEY","deviceName":"example-device","deviceSecret":"example-secret","port":"443","timeout_sec":5}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"remote_join","result":0,"code":0,"id":60}
```

Reply, bad-credentials - Returned for any credential parse failure:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"remote_join","error":"stack is already running","code":259,"id":61}
```
